supporting_observations.claim: The repeated HTTPS proxy requests in the supplied window are to updates.pixelforge-suite.com and are attributed by endpoint telemetry to the approved PixelForge updater. Requests recur at roughly five-minute intervals from 13:37:50 to 14:07:46; one request at 13:42:31 received status 407, while the other listed requests received status 200.
The PixelForge updater process was launched from its installed Program Files path under leo.martins, and created a temporary file during the observed activity.

A Dropbox updater ran briefly as SYSTEM, and shortly afterward the workstation queried x7k9m2.akamaized.net, which resolved to 151.101.25.122. The records do not establish that the updater made a connection to that domain.

The workstation made a successful network logon to WS-SOKAFOR-01 using sam.okafor credentials. The inventory identifies sam.okafor as the sole IT administrator and says remote administration is done only from WS-SOKAFOR-01, making this direction of activity noteworthy but not proof of misuse.
FILE-NWD-01 initiated an RPC connection to WS-LMARTINS-01. The available records show the connection but do not identify its purpose or the process or user responsible.
The repeated Kerberos and LDAP events shown identify the workstation computer account, and are not by themselves evidence of an interactive administrator session.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show HTTPS CONNECT destinations and tunnel metadata, not the encrypted request or response contents (for example, T046-00101 and T046-00157).
The supplied records do not show a Dropbox updater network connection; the DNS query alone does not establish which process caused it or what followed (T046-00119, T046-00124, T046-00126).
The records provided do not include the content of the SMB activity or the purpose and authentication context of the FILE-NWD-01-to-workstation RPC connection (T046-00008, T046-00011, T046-00069).
The supplied window contains no direct evidence of what was executed on WS-LMARTINS-01 by sam.okafor or whether the FILE-NWD-01 RPC activity was authorized (T046-00024, T046-00069).
claims_not_established: Whether the Dropbox updater was intentionally installed and authorized, or was introduced as part of malicious activity.
Whether x7k9m2.akamaized.net is related to Dropbox, another legitimate application, or malicious activity.
Whether sam.okafor's successful network logon from WS-LMARTINS-01 was authorized or involved administrative actions.
Whether the RPC connection from FILE-NWD-01 was legitimate maintenance or unauthorized remote activity.
Whether any data was transferred to an unapproved service or any payload was downloaded or executed.
Whether the activity caused compromise or persistence on the workstation.
additional_evidence_needed: Obtain endpoint process-to-network telemetry and application installation/signature details for DropboxUpdate.exe, including whether it initiated outbound connections.
Review proxy and DNS records around the Dropbox updater execution, including any subsequent connections to Akamai-hosted or other destinations.
Investigate the sam.okafor logon on WS-SOKAFOR-01: source authentication details, associated logon/session activity, and any resulting administrative actions.
Collect FILE-NWD-01 and WS-LMARTINS-01 RPC, SMB, and process telemetry around 13:31 UTC to determine the purpose and authorization of the remote connection.
Verify whether Dropbox was installed or approved for WS-LMARTINS-01 and correlate the PixelForge updater's observed update activity with vendor or software-management records.
